{{short description|Mathematical group}}
In mathematics, '''Nambooripad order'''<ref>{{cite book|last=Thomas Scott Blyth|title=Lattices and ordered algebraic structures|url=https://archive.org/details/latticesordereda00blyt_096|url-access=limited|year=2005|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-1-85233-905-0|pages=[https://archive.org/details/latticesordereda00blyt_096/page/n235 228]–232}}</ref>  (also called '''Nambooripad's partial order''') is a certain natural [[partial order]] on a [[regular semigroup]] discovered by [[K S S Nambooripad]]<ref>{{cite journal|last=K.S.S. Nambooripad|title=The natural partial order on a regular semigroup|journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society|year=1980|volume=23|issue=3|pages=249–260|doi=10.1017/s0013091500003801|doi-access=free}}</ref>  in late seventies. Since the same partial order was also independently discovered by Robert E Hartwig,<ref>{{cite journal|last=R. Hartwig|title=How to partially order regular elements|journal=Mathematica Japonica|year=1980|volume=25|issue=1|pages=1–13}}</ref>  some authors refer to it as '''Hartwig–Nambooripad order'''.<ref>{{cite journal|last=J.B. Hickey|title=On regularity preservation on a semigroup|journal=Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society|year=2004|volume=69|pages=69–86|doi=10.1017/s0004972700034274|doi-access=free}}</ref> "Natural" here means that the order is defined in terms of the operation on the semigroup.

In general Nambooripad's order in a regular semigroup is [[compatible operation|not compatible]] with multiplication. It is compatible with multiplication only if the semigroup is [[pseudo-inverse semigroup|pseudo-inverse]] (locally inverse).

== Precursors ==
Nambooripad's partial order is a generalisation of an earlier known partial order on the set of [[idempotent]]s in any [[semigroup]]. The partial order on the set ''E'' of idempotents in a semigroup ''S'' is defined as follows: For any ''e'' and ''f'' in ''E'',  ''e''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''f'' if and 
only if ''e''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ef''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''fe''.

Vagner in 1952 had extended this to [[inverse semigroup]]s as follows: For any ''a'' and ''b'' in an inverse semigroup ''S'', ''a''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''b'' if and only if ''a'' =  '' eb'' for some idempotent ''e'' in&nbsp;''S''. In the [[symmetric inverse semigroup]], this order actually coincides with the inclusion of partial transformations considered as sets.  This partial order is compatible with multiplication on both sides, that is, if ''a''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''b'' then ''ac''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''bc'' and ''ca''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''cb'' for all ''c'' in&nbsp;''S''.

Nambooripad extended these definitions to regular semigroups.

==Definitions (regular semigroup) ==
The partial order in a regular semigroup discovered by Nambooripad can be defined in several equivalent ways. Three of these definitions are given below. The equivalence of these definitions and other definitions have been established by Mitsch.<ref>{{cite journal|last=H. Mitsch|title=A natural partial order for semigroups|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|date=July 1986|volume=97|issue=3|pages=384|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1986-097-03/S0002-9939-1986-0840614-0/S0002-9939-1986-0840614-0.pdf|accessdate=11 April 2011|doi=10.1090/s0002-9939-1986-0840614-0 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Definition (Nambooripad)===

Let ''S'' be any regular semigroup and ''S''<sup>1</sup> be the semigroup obtained by adjoining the identity 1 to ''S''. For any ''x'' in ''S'' let ''R<sub>x</sub>'' be the [[Green's relations|Green R-class]]  of ''S'' containing ''x''. 
The relation ''R<sub>x</sub>''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''R<sub>y</sub>'' defined by ''xS''<sup>1</sup>&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;''yS''<sup>1</sup> is a partial order in the collection of [[Green's relations|Green R-classes]] in&nbsp;''S''.  For ''a'' and ''b'' in ''S'' the relation ≤ defined by

*''a'' ≤ ''b'' if and only if ''R<sub>a</sub>''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''R<sub>b</sub>'' and ''a'' = ''fb'' for some [[idempotent]] ''f'' in&nbsp;''R<sub>a</sub>''

is a partial order in ''S''. This is a natural partial order in&nbsp;''S''.

===Definition (Hartwig)===

For any element ''a'' in a regular semigroup ''S'', let ''V''(''a'') be the set of inverses of ''a'', that is, the set of all ''x'' in ''S'' such that ''axa''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''a'' and ''xax''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''x''. 
For ''a'' and ''b'' in ''S'' the relation ≤ defined by

*''a'' ≤ ''b'' if and only if ''a'a''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''a'b'' and ''aa' ''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ba' '' for some ''a' '' in&nbsp;''V''(''a'')

is a partial order in ''S''. This is a natural partial order in ''S''.

===Definition (Mitsch)===

For ''a'' and ''b'' in a regular semigroup ''S'' the relation ≤ defined by

*''a''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''b'' if and only if ''a''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''xa''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''xb''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''by''  for  some element ''x'' and ''y'' in&nbsp;''S''

is  a partial order in ''S''. This is a natural partial order in ''S''.

==Extension to arbitrary semigroups (P.R. Jones)==
For ''a'' and ''b'' in an arbitrary semigroup ''S'', ''a'' ≤<sub>J</sub> ''b'' iff there exist ''e'', ''f'' idempotents in S<sup>1</sup> such that ''a'' = ''be'' = ''fb''.

This is a reflexive relation on any semigroup, and if ''S'' is regular it coincides with the Nambooripad order.<ref name="Higg"/>

==Natural partial order of Mitsch ==
Mitsch further generalized the definition of Nambooripad order to arbitrary semigroups.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Peter M. Higgins|title=The Mitsch order on a semigroup|journal=[[Semigroup Forum]]|year=1994|volume=49|issue=1|pages=261–266|doi=10.1007/BF02573488}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Mario Petrich|title=Certain partial orders on semigroups|journal=Czechoslovak Mathematical Journal|year=2001|volume=51|issue=2|pages=415–432|url=http://dml.cz/bitstream/handle/10338.dmlcz/127657/CzechMathJ_51-2001-2_15.pdf|accessdate=11 April 2011|doi=10.1023/a:1013711417539|hdl=10338.dmlcz/127657|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

The most insightful formulation of Mitsch's order is the following. Let ''a'' and ''b'' be two elements of an arbitrary semigroup ''S''. Then ''a'' ≤<sub>M</sub> ''b'' iff there exist ''t'' and ''s'' in S<sup>1</sup> such that ''tb'' = ''ta'' = ''a'' = ''as'' = ''bs''.

In general, for an arbitrary semigroup ≤<sub>J</sub> is a subset of ≤<sub>M</sub>. For [[epigroup]]s however, they coincide. Furthermore, if ''b'' is a regular element of ''S'' (which need not be all regular), then for any ''a'' in ''S'' a ≤<sub>J</sub> b iff a ≤<sub>M</sub> b.<ref name="Higg">{{cite book|author=Peter M. Higgins|title=Techniques of semigroup theory|url=https://archive.org/details/techniquessemigr00higg_014|url-access=limited|year=1992|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-853577-5|pages=[https://archive.org/details/techniquessemigr00higg_014/page/n30 46]–48}}</ref>
